 Pick Six Previews: BYU's defense to hold Kansas en route to road win
 Posted - Nov. 20, 2026 at 12:49 p.m. 
 Brett Ciancia KSL Contributor    
  
  
  
 Save Story PROVO — BYU bounced back from the Utah loss with a dominant 28-7 win over Baylor. After firing head coach Dave Aranda, Baylor was on a hot streak and averaged 40+ points per game in the two prior to this one. BYU completely neutralized their explosive offense.
 Part of the formula was ball control by the offense. BYU dominated the time of possession, especially in the first half, by holding the ball 21 minutes to Baylor's nine. 
 Three of those long drives ended in Bear Bachmeier touchdown runs, where he became the first Big 12 quarterback since Patrick Mahomes (2016) to score three rushing touchdowns in a first half.
 The defense also did its job and held Baylor to under 100 yards through the first three quarters. Then, with the game 21-7 and Baylor attempting to gain momentum, BYU swarmed DJ Lagway for two sacks to stunt their comeback attempt.
 BYU is 8-2 and currently ranked in the College Football Playoff's projected field. They head to Lawrence to face a 4-6 Kansas team that is better than their record would indicate (10 a.m. MT, ABC).
 Game Grader
 (Opponent-adjusted statistical dominance via Pick Six Previews) 
 3-year average (2023-25): BYU 55.3 (28th of 68 Power 4) | Kansas 53.1 (30th)
 2025 season: BYU 63.4 (19th) | Kansas 44.2 (49th)
 2026 season: BYU 65.2 (17th) | Kansas 49.3 (42nd)
 My Game Grader formula is a measure of statistical dominance that adjusts for opponent strength and is a key piece of my preseason and in-season evaluation.
 In my annual season preview magazine Pick Six Previews, I selected BYU to finish second in the Big 12 race, with a No. 17 spot in the preseason top 25. After its 6-0 start and Notre Dame win, BYU moved up to No. 11 but have fell down to No. 17 with a pair of losses to UCF and Utah.
 I selected Kansas to finish 14th in the Big 12 and were a Pick Six PLUS win total pick to go under 5.5 wins. So far that has been accurate, and they check in with a 4-6 record and are in a tie for second-to-last in the conference.
 With that said, this team has performed better than their record would suggest, and my Game Grader formula has them at No. 42 overall, but No. 22 in the last four games. 
 BYU with the ball
 (Opponent-adjusted rankings via Pick Six Previews) 
 BYU offense: 26th of 68 Power 4
 Kansas defense: 29th of 68 Power 4
 Bachmeier tossed four interceptions against Utah but bounced back against Baylor. He played a clean game, scored all four touchdowns, and led with 54 rushing yards. All-Big 12 running back LJ Martin worked back into the lineup and had six carries for 49 yards, but then suffered an ankle injury near halftime.
 My opponent-adjusted rushing stats show the contrast of BYU with and without Martin in the backfield. With Martin (first three games), BYU ranked fifth in my opponent-adjusted rushing. But in the five games without him, they are just 45th of 68 Power Four teams.
 Though they didn't hit any long-yardage explosive passes against Baylor, their Joe Moore Award semifinalist offensive line was able to help sustain long drives that built the insurmountable 21-0 lead.
 The Kansas defensive line is a clear strength, and they will challenge the BYU front. They are registering a negative play (sack or tackle-for-loss) on 10% of snaps, which is high enough to rank 16th nationally.
 They are fresh off their best performance this season, where they held the high-powered West Virginia offense to just 14 points and 200 rushing yards below their per-game average.
 Kansas with the ball
 (Opponent-adjusted rankings via Pick Six Previews) 
 Kansas offense: 36th of 68 Power 4
 BYU defense: 3rd of 68 Power 4
 Which version of Kansas quarterback Isaiah Marshall will show up Saturday? Marshall has flashed some incredible highs, elusiveness in the pocket, speed on scrambles, and highlight-reel off-balance throws. At other times, like the Missouri second half, Arizona State game, and TCU second half, he has thrown costly interceptions that have flipped wins to losses.
 Kansas may hit a wild play or two, but on a down-to-down basis this side of the ball is a clear advantage for BYU's defense, which is ranked in the top 40 in every single stat category (except third-down conversions). BYU has one of the best defensive stat profiles in America, and in the most telling stat, my opponent-adjusted per-play, they are No. 3 overall.
 Game prediction
 BYU is back on track, and the defense is the best unit in this matchup. Look for BYU to disrupt the Kansas offense and force multiple turnovers. The Kansas defense may keep BYU in check through the first few quarters, but eventually BYU will hit an explosive play or two.
 Over the past three years, Kansas has had close game problems, going 3-10 in one-score games, with 12 blown fourth-quarter leads. Those trends continue and BYU will get to 9-2.
 BYU 24 | Kansas 17
